expected: Protocol-valid writes require HWRITE and HTRANS[1] to reach the registered write-data-phase qualifier together
notes: Retained open image reinterpreted as a complete coupled consumer footprint. The active selector codewords are common to all eight qualified write-group images. This does not isolate either signal alone; it qualifies their paired delivery into the write-data-phase LUT/register. The existing eight group records remain the primary functional observations.
observed: All eight protocol-valid HWDATA nibble campaigns passed 64/64 exact writes; group1 anchor FCB=0x000f0002 and lanes [4,5,6,7] exact 64/64

build_notes: Three flow requirements that cost a cycle each and are not obvious: cell NAMES carry the AHB lane (the packer parses hwdata<N>/h<N>), so a generate block naming instances lane[2].din fails with 'no known AHB input lane'; a portless top module needs an explicit (* top *) attribute or yosys leaves it un-elaborated with zero cells, which presents as a design that routes 0 arcs; and at least one interior FF-to-FF path is required or nextpnr reports no Fmax and the frequency check fails the build, since every capture lane otherwise runs pin-to-pin.
consequence: Corrects the standing attribution of the 8-bit writable ceiling. The joint MCU corridor allocator was NOT the wall -- 16 lanes routed first try. The wall was the direct-D admission envelope (four exact sites), which a hold-mux register consumes one per lane; sharing removes it entirely.
localization: The two failing lanes are exactly the two whose readback exits X13Y12_BBMUXE07 and X13Y12_BBMUXE11 (verified in the routed netlist; every other lane exits a different BBMUXE terminal and verifies exactly). BBMUXE07 is separately silicon-qualified for the BRAM x9 q5 corridor, so the terminal is not inherently broken -- it is this source/composition that fails on it.
next_experiment: Resolve lanes 5 and 9 by giving their BBMUXE terminals the treatment the GPIO5 boundary needed: check whether those two exit groups require an explicit terminal default that the current emission leaves unset for this source, comparing against the qualified BRAM x9 q5 image which drives BBMUXE07 successfully from a different source.
observed: A SIXTEEN-lane simultaneous writable image was built through the release uarch flow and read on silicon. It clears the direct-D envelope with zero own-Q cells (storage is an unconditional-capture flip-flop per lane, INIT=0xAAAA with D a plain buffer of the hard HWDATA pin, plus ONE shared write decode), routed on the FIRST attempt with no cap/fanout escalation, and emitted strict-clean: 212 data pips, 193 mapped, 0 unmapped, 0 predicted, 0 legacy. Timing PASS (644.33 MHz and 110.34 MHz against a 10 MHz target). On the board, using the same protocol-valid write/read pair oracle as the qualified per-group campaign: groups 0 and 3 PASS 64/64 exact (lanes 0-3 and 12-15), while groups 1 and 2 return 29/64 and 31/64 with lanes 5 and 9 not varying. The failing signature is unambiguous and reproducible across reruns: lane 5 reads 1 for every pattern regardless of what was written, likewise lane 9.
scope: Establishes that SIXTEEN simultaneous HWDATA lanes route, emit strict-clean and are readable, with 14 of 16 exact over 64 patterns each. It does NOT qualify a 16-bit register bank, and it is a NARROWER semantic than the qualified 8-bit bank: this is unconditional per-lane capture (a posted scratch) with one shared write decode, not the qualified bank's commit/wait/W1C state, and it retains a value only across the write-to-read turnaround. Lanes 5 and 9 are an open defect, not a pass. The qualified writable surface is unchanged by this record.

consequence: Two conclusions worth separating. (1) MECHANISM: hard-block boundary selectors are source-dependent, and emitting one encoding irrespective of the routed source silently produces a terminal that selects something other than what the design drives. This is the same defect shape as the top-edge pad failure, where padfeed_L48_top.csv names a feeder the vendor does not use, so the pad's IOMUX selects a node the design never drives -- one mechanism, two campaigns. (2) PROCESS: bitgen reported 212 pips, 193 mapped, 0 unmapped for this image. Strict-clean emission with zero unmapped selectors is therefore NOT sufficient to guarantee a correct boundary selector; the encoding was present and wrong, not missing. Any future 'strict-clean therefore correct' inference about a boundary terminal is unsafe.
next_experiment: Make boundary-terminal emission a function of the ACTUAL routed source and fail closed when the (source, terminal) pair has no witnessed encoding, rather than emitting a source-independent default. The harvest tooling for the pad side already exists (engine_work/harvest_pad_approach.py extracts vendor (source -> terminal) pairs from a routed vendor build); the same approach applies to BBMUXE. A cheap confirmation first: rebuild the 16-lane image with lane 5 forced onto RMUX63 (the source the qualified image uses) and re-read group 1.
observed: Localized the 16-lane stuck lanes to a SOURCE-DEPENDENT boundary selector, and refuted the first hypothesis on the way. Hypothesis tested and REJECTED: that BBMUXE needs the inactive-terminal treatment BBMUXS needs for GPIO5 -- the BBMUXE07 terminal cells are BIT-IDENTICAL between the qualified 8-bit bank image (lane 5 works) and the 16-lane capture image (lane 5 stuck), so no terminal default is missing. What differs is the SOURCE: in the qualified image BBMUXE07 is driven by X14Y12_RMUX63, in the 16-lane image by X14Y12_RMUX43, while the emitted terminal selector is the same in both. The same phenomenon is already on record from a different campaign, where the BRAM x9 work documented a source-dependent RMUX43-to-BBMUXE06 selector.
scope: Diagnostic record. No feature claim is added or widened; the two stuck lanes remain an open defect and the 16-lane image remains unqualified.

consequence: Lane 5 is explained and fixed at the mechanism level. The emitted BBMUXE07 codeword (0,6) is source RMUX63's, and in this very image X14Y12_RMUX63 carries $PACKER_VCC_NET -- which is why the failure signature was stuck HIGH specifically, not stuck low or noisy. Lane 9 is a SEPARATE defect: its exit X14Y12_RMUX26 -> X13Y12_BBMUXE11 is emitted as (1,4), which IS the harvested codeword for RMUX26, so the terminal is right and the cause lies elsewhere on that net -- most likely its route through X14Y12_RMUX73, a known MCU entry wire, and an RMUX -> IMUX -> RMUX detour at X14Y8.
correction_note: This supersedes the interpretation in boundary-selector-is-source-dependent-20260815, which is WITHDRAWN. That record claimed the BBMUXE07 terminal cells were bit-identical between the working qualified image and the stuck one; the comparison was vacuous. The probe looked up cells named 'BBMUXE07' while pips_mcuedge.csv names them 'BBMUXE7' unpadded, so it compared an empty set and reported zero differences. Decoded correctly the two images DO differ at that mux. The correct mechanism is not that boundary selectors are source-dependent in a way we cannot capture -- they are a clean function of the source track, harvested with 14/14 feeders at n_variants=1 in chipdb/bbmuxe_fanin.csv -- it is that the shipped hand-typed copy of that table disagreed with the shipped data file on two feeders and nothing compared them.
next_experiment: Lane 9: force cap[9] off X14Y12_RMUX73 and off the X14Y8 IMUX detour, or route BBMUXE11 from RMUX49/RMUX20 (both corpus-witnessed into BBMUXE11 at (13,12)), and re-read group 2.
observed: The 16-lane shared-capture route was re-packed with the corrected BBMUXE_PAIR and re-read, unchanged in every other respect (same routed netlist; the image differs by exactly 2 config bytes plus the 4 CRC bytes, and the changed bytes are the (13,12) BBMUXE07 selector [0,6] -> [1,6]). group0 exact=64/64 PASS, group1 exact=64/64 PASS lanes [4,5,6,7], group3 exact=64/64 PASS. group2 is unchanged at exact=31/64 with lanes [8,10,11]: lane 9 is still stuck high. 15 of 16 lanes now read exact.
scope: Still NOT a qualified 16-bit register bank: this is unconditional per-lane capture (a posted scratch) with one shared write decode, and lane 9 remains an open defect. The qualified writable surface is unchanged. What is established is that 16 simultaneous HWDATA lanes route, emit strict-clean, and read exact on 15 of 16 lanes.

consequence: Closes the unexplained 15-of-16 diagnostic ceiling without widening register-bank semantics. HWDATA9 was already 64/64 exact in the isolated four-lane oracle; the failing simultaneous image placed its capture at X15Y12 slice4, an exact bus-clocked site whose I0 through I3 HWDATA5 discriminators all previously read stuck high. Moving only capture9 to the silicon-live X14Y11 slice7 site, with collision-free observed selectors, restores all sixteen lanes. The retained routed checkpoint is now hash-pinned by pack_regression.json.
observed: Matched board A/B over 64 protocol-valid write/read patterns. The unchanged control reproduced exact HWDATA-to-HRDATA correlations on lanes 0..8 and 10..15, with lane9 stuck high. The relocated image configured with FCB 0x000f0002 and returned exact same-index correlations for every lane 0..15; HRDATA16 continued to mirror lane0 as the timing-liveness stage. Strict pack reports 206 routed data pips, 187 mapped, 0 unmapped, 0 predicted and 0 legacy-absolute selectors. SRAM only; board reset after each run; flash untouched.
scope: Qualifies one exact L48 sixteen-lane simultaneous POSTED CAPTURE checkpoint: sixteen unconditional bus-clocked HWDATA captures, one shared write-decode observer and matching HRDATA readback during the write-to-read turnaround. It is not a 16-bit register bank and does not qualify hold muxes, address decode, commit/wait/W1C semantics, reset, arbitrary placement, or fresh 16-lane routing. The complete qualified writable bank remains eight bits.
